title: Decider status.json fresh-git-base write discipline — source fix for the daily PROP-130 chimera
problem: PROP-130 (2026-07-11) accepted the status.json two-writer race as occasional and self-healing, choosing instrumentation-only. Under the quiet-period cadence the race is now DETERMINISTIC-DAILY, not occasional: three consecutive daily chimeras — 27bf1e4b (07-12), 19b70279 (07-13), 25a4825 (07-14) — each with the identical signature: the 04:0x UTC workspace-sync slot whole-file-pushes the FUSE copy of monitor/status.json over the same-day poller commit, reverting poll fields to 2026-07-10 content. Mechanism (poller's 07-15 hypothesis, confirmed by this run's audit): (1) status.json is workspace-owned in build.js OWNERSHIP (line 307), so it is EXCLUDED from every git-to-FUSE sync path (build.js sync-workspace, dome-mirror step4c) — the FUSE copy never receives poller's git-only poll-field commits and its poll fields are permanently frozen (currently at 07-10 content); (2) decider's daily ~02:2x UTC run read-modify-writes the FUSE copy (per decider-reporting.md Step 8, which today says only 'Update monitor/status.json ... if needed' — NO base-content discipline is specified anywhere in decider.md or its reference files), arming the mtime with stale poll fields; (3) workspace-sync at 04:0x sees FUSE mtime newer than git and publishes the chimera. Poller self-heals ~21h later and integrity's PROP-130 canary flags it, so each occurrence costs: one wrong-data day on status.json poll fields, one integrity finding, one ISS (ISS-2962 -> ISS-2981 -> ISS-2984), one decider triage cycle, and one poller restore — daily churn for a fix that is one prompt-paragraph away. The prevention layer designed for exactly this shape (PROP-129 CHECK 4 monotonic-timestamp guard in the workspace-sync pre-push hook) was authored 2026-07-11 and is still status=proposed / unimplemented (verified this run: lint-workspace-sync-push.js has CHECKs 1/2/3 only, verification_pattern returns STILL_BROKEN).

proposed_fix.summary: Two layers. Layer 1 (this PROP's edit): codify a fresh-git-base rule in decider-reporting.md Step 8 — decider must compose its status.json update on the clone's git-HEAD copy (which contains poller's latest commit), field-merge its own decider-owned fields into that base, and write the merged result to FUSE. This makes the content workspace-sync later publishes correct BY CONSTRUCTION, killing the chimera at its source with zero hot-path code. Decider already did this ad hoc on 2026-07-15 (commit 714e8f3, 'rebased onto fresh poller data to avoid PROP-130 chimera near-miss') — this PROP simply makes the good instinct mandatory. Layer 2 (escalation, no new authorship): operator should ratify + implement PROP-129 CHECK 4 as the enforcement backstop for the same shape arriving via any other writer; fail-open discipline per CHECK 3 precedent.

files_to_modify.replace:
## Step 8: Update Status

Update `monitor/status.json` and `monitor/review-state.json` if needed.

**status.json fresh-git-base rule (PROP-135, 2026-07-15 — chimera source fix).** status.json has two writers on two paths: poller commits poll fields git-only; you write run fields to the FUSE copy. The FUSE copy NEVER receives poller's git-only commits (status.json is workspace-owned, so every git-to-FUSE sync path skips it) — its poll fields are permanently stale. If you read-modify-write the FUSE copy's content, you arm the workspace-sync mtime with stale poll fields, and the next 04:0x UTC sync publishes a chimera that clobbers poller's same-day commit (the PROP-130 pattern: commits 27bf1e4b, 19b70279, 25a4825 — three consecutive days). Therefore, every time you update monitor/status.json:

1. **Base on git, not FUSE.** Read `monitor/status.json` from your fresh clone (git HEAD — it has poller's latest commit). Never use the FUSE copy's content as the base of your update.
2. **Field-merge.** Carry every poll-owned field (`last_poll`, `last_poll_note`, `last_poll_note_prev`, `consecutive_quiet_polls`, `changes_pending_analysis`) verbatim from the git base. Overwrite only decider-owned fields (`last_run`, `last_agent`, `run_type`, `mode`, `status`, `last_decider_*`, `prev_decider_run`, `open_issues*`, `issues_*`, `patches_applied_this_run`, `curmudgeon_*`, `notes_this_run`, `push_status`, `last_updated`).
3. **Newest-poll wins.** If the FUSE copy's `last_poll` is somehow NEWER than the git base's (poller landed between your clone and now), take the poll-owned fields from FUSE instead. Compare timestamps; never regress `last_poll` or `consecutive_quiet_polls`.
4. **Write the merged result to the FUSE copy** as usual (status.json stays workspace-owned; workspace-sync publishes it on its next slot).

This makes the file workspace-sync pushes correct by construction. PROP-129 CHECK 4 (monotonic guard in the ws-sync pre-push hook) is the enforcement backstop for the same shape from any other writer — pending operator ratification.
files_to_modify.explanation: Adds the missing write discipline at the exact step where decider is instructed to update status.json. No ownership reclassification, no hot-path hook code, no new scripts — a prompt-level source fix.

tradeoffs: Gain: eliminates the deterministic daily chimera at its source; zero code in workspace-sync's disaster-class hot path; no OWNERSHIP/classification churn; consistent with INST-4 direction PROP-130 already observed organically landing (dc46773, 714e8f3). Lose/risk: (a) prompt-level rules depend on LLM compliance — the historical skip-by-omission class (PROP-066) applies; mitigated because the rule sits inside Step 8 itself (not a separate late section) and PROP-129 CHECK 4, once ratified, catches non-compliance at push time; (b) if poller ever adds new poll-owned fields, the enumerated field list needs maintenance — the rule states the principle (poll-owned fields verbatim from git base) so drift degrades gracefully; (c) does not fix OTHER workspace-owned two-writer files — out of scope, none currently exhibit the daily-collision cadence. Alternative rejected this run: making dome-mirror copy status.json git-to-FUSE would create the reverse race (git base clobbering decider's fresh FUSE run-fields between decider write and workspace-sync push) and violates the workspace-owned classification; PROP-130's STRUCT-1/2/3 rejections (file split, single-writer refactor, semantic merge in sync hot path) remain sound — this PROP is cheaper than all three.
estimated_impact: Removes ~1 integrity finding + ~1 ISS + ~1 decider triage cycle + ~1 poller restore PER DAY under current cadence; removes the ~21h/day window where status.json poll fields are wrong at HEAD; closes ISS-2984 on application.

escalation_note_for_operator: Separately from this PROP: PROP-129 (CHECK 4 monotonic guard) has been sitting status=proposed since 2026-07-11 while the exact failure it prevents fired on 07-12, 07-13, and 07-14. Recommend ratifying/implementing it as the backstop layer even after PROP-135 applies.
